title: General divisors irreducible simultaneously on a finite etale cover
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $X$ a smooth connected affine $k$-scheme of finite type and pure dimension $d\ge2$, and $\pi:T\to X$ a finite etale morphism with $T$ connected. Let $S\subset X(k)$ be a nonempty finite set. Let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module, $V$ a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space, and $\psi:V\to\Gamma(X,L)$ a $k$-linear map. Assume all $\psi(v)$ vanish on the reduced subscheme $S$, their restrictions generate $L|_{X\setminus S}$, and the associated morphism $X\setminus S\to\mathbf P(V)$ is an immersion. For $v\in V$ set $H_v=Z(\psi(v))$ and $T_v=T\times_X H_v$. There is a nonempty Zariski open $U_{\rm irr}\subseteq\mathbf A(V)$ such that both $H_v$ and $T_v$ are geometrically irreducible over $k$ for every $v\in U_{\rm irr}(k)$. For such a $v$, if $H_v$ is smooth over $k$, then $T_v$ is smooth over $k$, and $T_v\to H_v$ is a finite etale morphism between connected schemes. Here $\mathbf A(V)$ is affine space with $k$-points $V$. Scheme and morphism notions are those of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]; invertible sheaves, generation, associated projective morphisms, zero schemes, base change and connectedness are as in [def-sc-invertible-module], [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections], [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections], [def-pc-zero-scheme], [def-pc-base-change] and [def-weil-connected-scheme]; geometric irreducibility is as in [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]; pure dimension is as in [def-weil-pure-dimension].

proof.text: Both X and T are smooth over k and connected. Over an algebraically closed (hence separably closed) field, connectedness implies geometric connectedness by the proved source theorem. A smooth geometrically connected morphism is geometrically irreducible by GeometricallyIrreducible.of_smooth_of_geometricallyConnected, also proved in the source regular-scheme module. This replaces the finite-separable tensor test.

Form LT = pi*L by tensor pullback and psiT using tensorSectionsUnit. The adjunction comparison identifies this pullback with the usual pullback, proves invertibility, and identifies zero schemes. The scalar identity for psi and naturality of the unit make psiT k-linear. Its domain still has the given finite basis.

Apply the base-codimension lemma on T and use d >= 2 for the base-condition inequality. The transverse-component lemma verifies the other geometric hypothesis of irreducible Bertini. This gives one nonempty coefficient open for the pulled-back system on T; no second application on X is needed.

Expanding v in the given basis and using the scalar identity identifies psi(v) with the parameter combination. The unit preserves sums and the compatible scalars. The self-field base change is canonically isomorphic to the original scheme. Ideal-sheaf comapIso then identifies the pulled-back zero scheme with the chosen categorical pullback Tv. Transport geometric irreducibility through these isomorphisms.

The finite etale map pi has open and closed image in connected X. Its nonempty source makes that image nonempty, hence all of X, so pi is surjective. The restriction Tv -> Hv is its base change and is surjective. The proved source theorem GeometricallyIrreducible.of_surjective descends geometric irreducibility from Tv to Hv. Thus the single open for T already works simultaneously for both schemes.

The restriction Tv -> Hv is the base change of pi and is therefore finite etale. If Hv is smooth, compose this smooth etale restriction with its structure map. Specializing the two geometric irreducibility assertions to the base field gives irreducible, hence connected, source schemes.

proof_origin.place: Paragraph 3, implemented with one application of BertiniIrreducibleMember, the proved base-codimension lemma, and the separate transverse-component argument. Surjectivity of a nonempty finite etale cover and the proved source GeometricallyIrreducible.of_surjective replace the second Bertini application and intersection of parameter opens. Source geometric-connectedness and coheight APIs replace the finite-separable and finite-Artinian-support detours.

split_report.summary: Proved the original statement with no change and no new nodes. Reused the existing Bertini criterion and supplied its hypotheses on both schemes using regular local rings, the rational unramified cotangent criterion, Nakayama, height bounds and localization prime correspondence. Distinguished the support of the finite base locus from its possibly nonreduced scheme structure. Checked the actual project Bertini declaration, which is sorried and is a different statement. Repair after live-DAG promotion refusal: rebased the retained split onto the current unsplit item; compared all 36 cited statements with the retained full-statement citation quotes (all unchanged), rechecked every use and replaced the generic off-unit tool explanations with step-specific justifications. split_report.blueprint: Paragraph 3 of lem-zl-bertini-finite-cover-curve.proof.md: smooth connected implies irreducible; codimension of finite base loci; independent differentials; a codimension-two component avoiding the third divisor; simultaneous Bertini opens. Paragraph 4: smooth finite etale connected restriction.

tool_uses.why: Steps 1 and 11 use the flat-base-change identity and the affine quotient description of zero schemes. These are generic zero-scheme tools, not a different Bertini route; this unit has no lemma giving those formulas.

Steps 2, 5 and 15 use that an etale morphism is smooth and its fibres have dimension zero, to obtain regularity, finite base support and conditional smoothness upstairs. This unit has no such general etale geometry lemma.
Step 2 uses regularity of every local ring of a smooth scheme over a field. The unit has no general smooth-to-regular statement; this supplies local algebra for the prescribed Bertini argument.

Step 2 uses integrality of a nonempty connected regular scheme on both X and T. This is the general scheme-theoretic input for the blueprint sentence that both are irreducible; no statement in this unit supplies it.

Step 4 uses that closed points of finite-type schemes over k have residue fields finite over k, and that rational points are closed. This checks the rational-point hypotheses of the local cotangent tool; the unit has no closed-point field lemma.

Step 4 uses equality of the dimensions of a finite-type domain and its localization at any maximal ideal. This checks codimensions and cotangent dimensions at closed points, rather than replacing any unit-level argument.
Step 4 uses equality of local-ring dimensions along an etale ring map to obtain dimension d at closed points of T. The unit has no general dimension comparison for etale morphisms.

Steps 5 and 7 use the equivalence between generation of an invertible sheaf and some section being nonzero in every fibre. This identifies the base support and selects a frame; the unit contains no fibrewise generation criterion.

Step 7 uses polynomial affine coordinates and the section-ratio formulas on a projective chart to deduce cotangent spanning from the assumed immersion. This coordinate tool is not supplied by a statement of this unit.

Step 9 uses cotangent surjectivity for an unramified morphism at rational points. This proves that the same two section coefficients give independent directions upstairs; the unit contains no unramified cotangent criterion.
Step 10 uses regularity and dimension d-c of the quotients by the first c parameters. This is the local algebra proving the codimension-two witness in the blueprint, not a new Bertini conclusion.
Step 10 uses that each of the regular local rings R, R/(f) and R/(f,g) is a domain, making the parameter ideals prime. The unit has no general regular-local-domain theorem.
